biography: Leandro Romera, a Sao Paulo native, traded the chaos of the favelas for the controlled chaos of the racetrack. His introduction to motorsport was accidental - stumbling upon an illegal street race at age 15. The raw energy of the engines ignited a passion within him, a stark contrast to the poverty that defined his early life. He started with go-karts, funded by scavenging scrap metal and sheer determination. Early races were marked by aggressive maneuvers born of desperation, quickly earning him a reputation as a 'street brawler' on the track. Copa Montana offered him his first real shot, recognizing raw talent beneath the rough exterior. Now at 23, Romera is still proving himself. He is fighting to shake off his early reputation, aiming for consistency and strategic racing while retaining the fire that brought him this far.
drivingStyle: Romera's driving style reflects his defensive personality and his street racing origins. He's known for his incredibly late braking and his uncanny ability to defend his position, often frustrating more experienced drivers. He excels in close-quarters combat, using his car like a shield to protect his line. Tire management is an area he's actively working on; years of aggressive driving have ingrained a tendency to push too hard, too early, often leading to a drop in pace towards the end of races. He struggles under pressure, sometimes cracking when leading late in a race.

rivalries.reason: Silva, a veteran Copa Montana driver, publicly criticized Romera's aggressive driving style, calling it 'dangerous and unprofessional'. Their on-track battles are always intense and frequently involve contact.

Costa is a rising star in Copa Montana, and their rivalry is based on a constant battle for position. Both drivers are fiercely competitive and see each other as their biggest obstacle to championship contention.

Oliveira, known for his calculated and clean racing, embodies everything Romera is not. Their different approaches to racing often clash, leading to strategic battles on the track and passive-aggressive remarks off it.

quirks: Always wears the same faded 'Senna Sempre' t-shirt under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific samba song track on repeat for 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to eat anything red on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "They say I drive dirty? I say I drive hungry. And I'm starving."
careerHighlight: Finishing 3rd at the Interlagos Copa Montana race after starting in 15th position. This was his first podium finish and validated his potential to climb the ranks.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the last lap of the Curitiba race due to excessive tire wear, costing him his first career win.
